<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is an AUR wrapper package for the `gaze-gui` binary distributed by Gudu Labs. The `source` array fetches a `.pkg.tar.zst` archive from `https://packages.gundulabs.com/arch/packages/`, which is the package's own declared upstream host (consistent with `url="https://gaze.gundulabs.com"`). This is expected behavior for a binary distribution package.

The only code that executes during `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` is: (a) downloading the source archive, (b) extracting it to `$srcdir`, and (c) sourcing the PKGBUILD's top-level scope. The top-level scope contains only standard variable assignments (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `arch`, `source`, `sha256sums`, etc.) — there are no command substitutions, `eval`, `curl`/`wget` calls, or other executable constructs at the top level. There is no `pkgver()` function defined, so nothing in that hook can run. The archive is extracted via `makepkg`'s built-in extraction (using `bsdtar` for `.tar.zst`), which writes files to disk without executing them — this is the intended behavior of these commands and is explicitly within the designed scope of the gate.

A SHA-256 checksum is provided (not SKIP), and even if it were SKIP, that would not be grounds to fail this gate per the instructions. The `package()` function (which runs `bsdtar -xpf` and `find -delete`) only executes during the packaging phase, which is skipped by `--nobuild`/`--noprepare`. No genuinely malicious behavior (data exfiltration, execution of remote code, obfuscation, or system modification outside the package's scope) is present in anything that runs during the specified commands.
</details>
<evidence>

PKGBUILD safe for source-fetch/sourcing gate; no malicious top-level or pkgver code.</summary>
